title: Redesign the recovery-batch hold tests to catch a scan under the state lock without depending on the host's scheduler
outcome: The recovery-batch hold tests detect a real regression, a scan under the state lock, and tolerate a thread pausing briefly, so they are enabled again and pass on Windows and on DL560 under parallel tests. Which of DL560's holds of tens of milliseconds are on-CPU work under the lock is answered by measurement; why the off-CPU ones sleep is left to w-d9c86985a960.
acceptance: A note states from measurement, using the instrumented runs test-6be61b30 and test-f65ca018, which DL560 holds were on-CPU work under the state lock and which were off-CPU, naming the hold sites, and says the earlier runs test-e20b4f55, test-789dfcf3 and test-49895a93 were not instrumented. What the thread sleeps on while off-CPU, and whether that is a product finding, is left to w-d9c86985a960 and is not settled here.

The redesigned tests, the active-batch test and the empty-batch test, bound the median of each call's worst hold at 50 ms. They fail when the old session-table scan under the state lock is reintroduced, shown by a recorded failing run that reports the medians, and pass when a thread is forcibly paused during a hold in under half the calls. The oracle no longer takes each call's worst hold and then the second-worst of 100 calls. The test's comment states the known weakness in words: a scan under 50 ms is not caught.

The active-batch test is no longer ignored and the redesigned tests pass in a full gate on Windows and in a full gate on DL560, after repeated passes in the wide process on DL560 with the run count and the load recorded; the gate of the modeled parallel fixture in state_lock_parallel.rs is unchanged
The review pair has no outstanding finding of Medium or higher and the full gate is green on the exact candidate

completion.summary: The recovery-batch hold tests now bound the median of each call's worst hold at 50 ms, catch a reintroduced session-table scan, tolerate a paused thread in half the calls or fewer, and are no longer ignored. Landed in 91a3da13 with full gates on Windows B and DL560. Known weakness, stated in the test: a scan under the bound, or one slowing half the calls or fewer, isn't caught. Why threads sleep under the lock stays with w-d9c86985a960. Acceptance evaluation not requested, per Greg's rule (memory greg-acceptance-evaluation-non-blocking-2026-11-02).
